title: Tenant burst governor and reservation rightsizing playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description: Summary: Following the cluster capacity incident on 2026-03-10 (INC-2026-03-10-09) where a single tenant's ephemeral burst caused sustained eviction pressure and degraded SLAs for multiple customers, this ticket defines a concrete playbook to implement a tenant-level burst governor and an automated reservation rightsizing pipeline. Goal: limit short-term burst amplification, prevent reservation starvation, and provide a data-driven recommendation engine for reservation sizing to avoid future capacity storms while maintaining developer expectations for burst behavior. Outcome: reduce eviction spikes by >80% for noisy bursts, restore p95 latency SLO for impacted tenants, and provide operators with safe remediation steps and observability during incidents.
action_items: Implement tenant burst governor (token-bucket style) in allocation layer with configurable window and refill rate
Add 'sustained-utilization' metric (5m/1h) and expose in Console per-tenant dashboard
Build rightsizing job that analyzes per-tenant sustained qps, p95 token usage, and KV cache hit-rate to recommend reservation adjustments
Create emergency isolation knob to move offending tenant to isolated pool and trigger notification routing
Add autoscaling guardrail: limit burst amplification factor and backoff when eviction_rate > threshold
Integration tests: simulate concurrent bursts across tenants to validate governor and prevent regressions
Run slow rollout: alpha on canary cluster -> dedicated staging -> 25% of production -> full rollout
Add post-deploy dashboards and alerting rules: tenant_burst_tokens, reservation_utilization_pct, eviction_rate, p95_tail_latency
runbook_excerpt: 1) Identify top 5 tenants by tenant_burst_tokens_per_min and eviction_rate_per_node (Grafana link below)
2) If a tenant shows > 3x baseline sustained_utilization for > 10m, enable isolation knob and move to 'burst-sandbox' pool
3) If eviction_rate_per_node > 0.5% and p95_latency increased by > 2x, scale capacity and notify on-call runtime team
4) Apply short-term reservation increase for impacted tenants (automated via rightsizing job with manual approval), then monitor for 30m
5) If isolation repeated > 2x in 24h, require root-cause analysis and schedule quota/hard-limit policy
comments: 2026-03-12 Maya Chen: Initial writeup after postmortem readout. Captured root cause: unconstrained short-term burst from a training adapter which bypassed client-side rate-limiting and overwhelmed node-level KV cache eviction.
2026-03-12 Diego Alvarez: Proposed design for governor: token-bucket per-tenant with adjustable refill and burst-cap, enforced at allocator. Added emergency isolation knob concept.
2026-03-13 Priya Nair: Observability request: expose reservation_utilization_pct and tenant_kv_cache_miss_rate as first-class metrics; will attach Grafana panels.
2026-03-13 Luke Ford: Prototype PR opened (link above). PR contains allocator hooks and unit tests for token accounting. Needs load tests and e2e in staging.
2026-03-14 SRE Team: Validated prototype under synthetic burst harness; eviction spikes reduced 87% in canary cluster. SRE requests an automatic rollback plan and a feature flag for staged rollout.
2026-03-14 Product: Confirmed customer-facing message and compensation plan for degraded customers; include wording in postmortem.
2026-03-14 Diego Alvarez: Next steps: (1) finish rightsizing job and approval flow (2) add alerting thresholds (3) schedule rollout for 2026-03-22 canary window
acceptance_criteria: Production canaries show eviction_rate reduced by >= 80% vs baseline for synthetic bursts
No customer p95 latency regressions caused by governor within 2x of pre-incident levels
Rightsizing job produces recommendation report with historical 7d, 30d, and sustained-utilization metrics and a one-click apply flow (with audit log)
Operator runbook validated in at least two incident simulations and documented in Confluence
Feature flagged rollout and automatic rollback on >2% cluster-wide eviction_rate increase
notes: Design trade-offs considered: conservative governor limits vs developer UX. We will provide a 'burst credit' affordance for trusted tenants with VerifiedBurst label.
Longer-term work: integrate with billing to offer burst addons and surface cost implications in Console; explore kernel scheduling improvements to reduce per-tenant KV cross-talk.
Mitigations already applied: temporary tenant-level soft-quota applied to offender, and emergency reservation bump for impacted customers on 2026-03-11
